subject: Model takes 42s to run but trial validation with one iteration takes 18s...why?

messages.author: d640f02d29e7de63
messages.subject: Model takes 42s to run but trial validation with one iteration takes 18s...why?
parts:
Hello,

My model:

system.time(AreaBurnHarv_nb<-gmultmix(~LAREA_0000+REBU_0300+REGS_0300,~1,~1,data=umfGMM,mixture="NB")) #42s

runs in 42 seconds but trial validation of that model with one iteration:

system.time(GofAreaBurnHarv_pb<-parboot(AreaBurnHarv_nb,fitstats,nsim=1,report=1)) #19s

runs in 19 seconds.

Of course, the validation statistics with one iteration are meaningless, but doesn't parboot() still have fit the model (plus do a bunch of other things, e.g. ,simulate a dataset). So, shouldn't the validation, if anything, take longer than running the model...not less than half the time? 

Maybe I should be happy, because validation with 1000 iterations will take ~ 5 hours instead of >11, but it's a red flag that I'd like to sort out before proceeding.

Does anyone know what might be causing the discrepancy?

Many thanks,

Mark B.
Ph.D. Candidate
University of Saskatchewan

messages.author: 403be63af7ebf220
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Model takes 42s to run but trial validation with one iteration takes 18s...why?
parts:
Hi Mark,

parboot uses se=FALSE when it fits the model to the simulated data sets. This saves a lot of time because the hessian matrix isn't computed. 

Richard

messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] Model takes 42s to run but trial validation with one iteration takes 18s...why?
parts:
Dear all,

and the general thing to be learnt from this is that whenever you do not need the standard errors, you can switch them off in the model fitting by putting se=FALSE, and you will typically get your results in about half of the time. Examples where you don't need the SE's are many exploratory analyses and also when you want to get the AIC for a set of models.

Best regards  ---  Marc
